title: Session 1 — Participant 1 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Creating a video from my iPhone footage
context: I want to make a quick family video edit for myself. And so I will use Claude to help me gather ideas, especially from its interpretation of my transcript.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes. Using the workflow + Claude, I was able to get my 4-Minute video done. I took suggestions from Claude, including the music choices and how to structure and end the video.

Step 1.step_name: Upload footage from iPhone to computer
Step 1.step_action: I will use Airdrop to put my footage onto the computer, and organize all the files the best that I can.

nodes.label: Narrate retrospective self-assessment of the completed footage transfer
nodes.detail: The AirDrop transfer from iPhone to computer was already completed before recording started, so the user faces the camera and narrates a retrospective self-rating: footage quality, upload speed, and organization all went well (rated 5/5), with the only friction being manually sorting footage from multiple cameras.

Step 2.step_name: Gather transcripts from Premiere Pro AND place it in Claude
Step 2.step_action: Placing footage into Premiere Pro and getting a transcript for Claude to understand. I then export the .srt file from Premiere Pro. I would then have Claude interpret the transcript.

nodes.label: Organize imported footage and run speech-to-text transcription
nodes.detail: Organizes roughly 120 imported clips onto a RAW timeline in Premiere Pro and runs Premiere's built-in Speech to Text feature on the footage to generate a working transcript.

nodes.label: Attempt a voiceover narration take recapping the birthday
nodes.detail: Creates a dedicated 'RAW NARRATION' sequence and records an out-loud voiceover recapping the day's events (breakfast, mall, movie, Vision Pro demo), but stumbles partway through and cuts the take short.

nodes.label: Notice mistakes and redo the narration take
nodes.detail: Judges the first take unusable ('mistake on human error'), starts recording again, but this second attempt is also flagged as not quite right; the timeline shows multiple distinct narration clips accumulating from these repeated attempts.

nodes.label: Record a complete, clean narration take
nodes.detail: Records a full clean take of the birthday recap voiceover start to finish, then reviews it in the Essential Sound panel with speech enhancement and repair settings applied.

nodes.label: Generate and export a caption sidecar file from the narration
nodes.detail: Troubleshoots an initial captions problem (audio was muted), then runs 'Create Captions from Transcript' and exports only a caption sidecar (.srt) file rather than the full video, since only the captions are needed.

nodes.label: Narrate retrospective self-rating for the transcription step
nodes.detail: Rates this step a 4 out of 5 to camera, explaining it took a little longer than expected but that Premiere's transcription and the upcoming AI assistance saved significant time versus captioning manually.

nodes.label: Upload the transcript to Claude and request editing guidance
nodes.detail: Opens a new Claude chat, attaches the exported .srt transcript, and asks for editing pointers, giving context that it's a 30th-birthday video wanting a 'chill but exciting' tone, and asking for bonus song suggestions.

nodes.label: Provide structural editing feedback and song suggestions
nodes.detail: Identifies the footage as having 'five mini-chapters,' praises the natural unscripted narration, flags that the video currently ends three separate times and should be trimmed to one ending, and proposes a chill-to-exciting song arc for each segment of the video.

nodes.label: Review Claude's feedback and decide to proceed to editing
nodes.detail: Reads through Claude's suggestions approvingly, decides song licensing doesn't matter since it's a personal video, and heads back to Premiere Pro to begin cutting based on the suggested chapter structure.

Step 3.step_action: Using the advice from Claude for inspiration, I will edit the video to my liking. (Output: Final Cut, with Claude's suggestions)

nodes.label: Begin trimming footage into a rough cut following Claude's structure
nodes.detail: Starts cutting the raw footage down toward a single-ending rough cut per Claude's chapter guidance, but deliberately overrides one suggestion — keeping in a couple of narration false-starts and stumbles Claude recommended cutting, judging that they add spontaneity.

nodes.label: Continue trimming and arranging the remaining footage into the rough cut
nodes.detail: Continues working through the rest of the footage — the mall, bookstore, theater, and Vision Pro segments — arranging clips into a coherent rough-cut sequence.

nodes.label: Regenerate captions to match the updated rough cut
nodes.detail: Re-runs 'Create Captions from Transcript' and re-exports the caption file now that the rough cut has reshaped the footage's timing, since the earlier captions no longer line up.

nodes.label: Re-upload captions to Claude for rough-cut review
nodes.detail: Uploads the captions file to Claude with the message 'I made a rough cut of my captions,' but (per the chat log) mistakenly re-sends the same unedited original file rather than the actual trimmed version.

nodes.label: Flag the re-uploaded file as unchanged and ask for clarification
nodes.detail: Per the chat log, Claude notices the re-upload is byte-for-byte identical to the original ('same 141 lines... did the trim not save?') and asks whether the user meant to upload a different version, restating the prior recommendations as a reminder. No Claude window is visible on screen at this point (the interaction happens off-camera, likely a second device), but the user's on-camera reaction moments later ('oh that's weird, I'm not sure why it didn't upload the real one, at least it told me that') directly matches this response, confirming it occurred.

nodes.label: Recognize the mistake and re-upload the actual rough-cut file
nodes.detail: Reacts on camera to Claude's response, realizes the wrong file was sent, and re-uploads the real trimmed captions file ('30th Birthday Captions RC1.srt') this time.

nodes.label: Deliver detailed second-round feedback on the rough cut
nodes.detail: Per the chat log, Claude analyzes the real RC1 rough cut: praises the runtime cut (8:36 to ~3:50), the merged recaps, the trimmed Vision Pro sequence, and the shirt-flip ending; flags four remaining issues (a garbled caption ~0:25-0:34, an unclear line ~2:59-3:04, an abrupt ending, and an optional recap tightening); and gives updated music cue points by timestamp. As with n15, this exchange is not visible on screen but is directly confirmed by the timestamped chat log.

nodes.label: Apply Claude's feedback to the rough cut
nodes.detail: Applies the fixes from Claude's second-round feedback back in Premiere: merges the two mall recaps, cuts the restaurant-decision section, corrects the Build-A-Bear/Nintendo mislabel, and fixes the flagged transcription error.

nodes.label: Select and preview music for each segment, adapting Claude's song suggestions
nodes.detail: After a brief pause acknowledging the session is running long, navigates to the music folder and works through Claude's suggested song arc for each segment, previewing tracks on YouTube and substituting personal picks where preferred — e.g. choosing MGMT's 'Kids' over 'Electric Feel' since it felt more fitting turning 30, plus SZA's 'Good Days', the Odyssey's 'Siren Song', 'Can You Hear the Music' from Oppenheimer, and Donna Lewis's 1996 song for period nostalgia instead of Claude's ending picks.

nodes.label: Download chosen tracks and generate instrumental versions
nodes.detail: Downloads the audio for each selected song and runs them through an online vocal-remover tool to produce instrumental versions, troubleshooting a couple of tool-loading glitches along the way.

nodes.label: Apply a music-ducking preset and place instrumentals under the narration
nodes.detail: Applies a 'Vocal Duck Male' audio preset, lowering the music roughly 8 dB under the narration, and places each instrumental track onto its corresponding segment across the timeline.

nodes.label: Review the edited timeline with music across an extended playback
nodes.detail: Plays back long stretches of the edited cut with music and narration together, checking transitions and timing, including intentionally timing one song's ending to a snap-of-the-fingers moment in the footage.

nodes.label: Reflect on final song choices relative to Claude's suggestions
nodes.detail: Summarizes to camera how each final song choice relates to what Claude originally suggested, explaining the reasoning behind each substitution made.

nodes.label: Add a title graphic to open the video
nodes.detail: Uses Premiere's title tool to add a 'Happy 30th Birthday!' title graphic near the intro, adjusting the font and size and adding a cross-dissolve transition.

nodes.label: Notice and fix a pitch-shift artifact on an instrumental track
nodes.detail: Notices the 'Kids' instrumental clip has an unintended pitch shift, catches it near the very end of the edit, and applies the Pitch Shifter audio effect to correct it.

nodes.label: Final playback review and confirm satisfaction with the video
nodes.detail: Does a final playback pass over the finished timeline and states on camera that they feel satisfied with the video; no on-screen export/render action occurs before the recording ends.

Step 1.step_name: Upload footage from iPhone to computer

rubrics: The quality of the footage is consistent with the original source
The speed of the upload is fast enough for me to jump into the project
The footage is organized in a way that Premiere Pro is able to sort it out on my timeline.

ratings.output_quality_reason: I was able to get all my footage onto the computer

goal_achievement.Why or why not: No; because I didn’t need Claude to do my task.

Step 2.step_name: Gather transcripts from Premiere Pro AND place it in Claude
Step 2.step_action: Placing footage into Premiere Pro and getting a transcript for Claude to understand. I then export the .srt file from Premiere Pro. I would then have Claude interpret the transcript.
rubrics: Captions are precisely synchronized with the dialogue and appear/disappear at appropriate times
Correct SRT format with properly structured subtitle entries and timestamps
Claude suggestions make sense to the editor at hand

ratings.output_quality_reason: I didn’t give it a perfect “5” because Premiere Pro didn’t perfectly transcribe the video. But Claude was helpful in enabling me to suit the video.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Because the transcription on Premiere Pro saved me a lot of time. If I were to try to do the captions manually, it would have taken me forever. Claude was able to give me great suggestions.

Step 3.output: Rough Cut 1 (without music); Final Cut (with Claude’s suggestions)

Claude suggestions make sense to the editor at hand
The final cut is to the quality that the editor wants to see
